subject: Private Offer — split activation & approval sequencing for pilot
messages:
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@acmehealth.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private Offer — sequencing question for pilot activation

Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the model latency and cost numbers looked promising for our triage workflow. Before procurement takes the PO path, two quick questions from our side about private-offer structure:

1) Can we split the private offer so the initial 3-month pilot (50 seats) is approved by a single BU approver, and the full activation (enterprise-wide) requires cross-BU procurement signoff?
2) If we do staged activation, can we gate billing for the second tranche until the enterprise PO is signed?

Procurement@acmehealth.com are copied. We're trying to avoid multiple legal redlines before the pilot. If you can sketch the approval/activation sequence and any recommended term/tenor constraints, that would help speed our internal review.

— Alex
Alex Jenkins
Head of Platform Integrations, Acme Health

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@acmehealth.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-29T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer — sequencing question for pilot activation

Hi Alex — appreciate the clarity. Short answers up front: yes, and yes, with a couple of guardrails.

Sketch below (high level):
- Phase A (Pilot): private offer created for 3 months, 50 seats, single-BU approval (buyer champion signoff). Billing active on Day 1 for only Phase A usage.
- Phase B (Enterprise activation): separate acceptance event triggers expansion of seat entitlement and cross-BU procurement approval; billing for Phase B begins only after enterprise PO is uploaded/accepted (DocuSign or marketplace purchase order).
- Contract/tenor recommendation: keep Phase A as a time-limited pilot (90 days) with an option to convert into a 12-month usage commitment to avoid multiple redlines. For pricing, we can use a short-term pilot rate plus an optional annual committed discount schedule.

Operational notes:
- We will put the buyer entitlement in the private-offer metadata so marketplace activation is tied to the accepted DocuSign/PO id.
- If procurement needs an invoice hold until enterprise PO is signed, we can support staged billing in our billing system (hold on expand). Finance and legal will want to confirm hold language.

I'm attaching a draft MPO terms doc to show how we'd articulate pilot constraints and activation triggers. Vanessa/vivek — can you weigh in on finance/legal constraints and whether the billing hold is doable from your perspective?

Next steps: if this sketch looks OK, I'll send a version with explicit acceptance checklist and scalable pricing bands.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Account Executive — AWS Marketplace & Co-sell, Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T08:21:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Private Offer — sequencing question for pilot activation

Forwarding Alex's ask and Rishi's sketch. Quick internal notes:

On Fri, Nov 29, 2026 at 11:03 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
> (see sketch)

Finance/legal checkpoints we need to cover before committing to a billing "hold" architecture:
- Legal: avoid open-ended liability if Phase B is delayed; define a clear expiration (e.g., 90 days to convert) and what happens to consumed pilot usage if conversion doesn't occur.
- Finance: we can implement a staged billing approach where Phase A invoices are issued on standard net-30 and Phase B invoices are blocked until PO/DocuSign reference is recorded. That requires marking the MPO record and a manual trigger in finance to lift the block. Not ideal for scale, but acceptable for a single enterprise pilot.

Attachments: pricing-schedule.xlsx with suggested short-term pilot pricing and post-conversion committed tiers.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Revenue Operations & Finance, Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-03T13:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer — sequencing question for pilot activation

Agree with Vanessa. A couple of operational clarifications:
- We'll add an MPO metadata field named "activation_trigger_doc" that stores the DocuSign/PO id. Expansion APIs will check that field before enabling extra seats.
- For billing: finance will generate invoices for Phase A as usual. We'll add a one-line hold comment for Phase B invoices and require the PO id to be present before release.
- Risk: this is slightly manual and adds a step for our billing ops — recommend we include a $0.00 trial/activation check to verify entitlement before billing to prevent accidental charges.

Action items for Rishi:
1) Finalize MPO language for the pilot activation trigger and share with Alex.
2) If accepted, initiate the MPO in AWS with Phase A entitlements and provide the MPO id to Acme.

— Vivek
Director, Cloud Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-11T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer — sequencing question for pilot activation

Alex / Procurement team —

Thanks for the prompt responses. Attached is a short MPO terms sheet and the pilot pricing schedule (see attachments). High-level proposal:

- MPO id: we will provision MPO-ACME-0926 (placeholder) for Phase A — 90-day pilot, 50-seat entitlement, billing enabled for Phase A only.
- Activation condition for Phase B: signed enterprise PO or DocuSign reference captured in the MPO metadata. Once we receive the PO id, Redwood will flip the activation flag and billing for the expanded seats will start.
- If Acme elects not to convert at the end of 90 days, consumed usage will be invoiced pro-rata; no automatic renewal.

Next steps:
1) Alex — confirm acceptance of pilot terms by EOD Friday and provide buyer champion name for single-BU approval.
2) Procurement — if you want the billing hold language changed, send legal redline back to vanessa@redwood.com.
3) On acceptance, I will create the MPO in AWS and share the MPO id and a DocuSign agreement link for signature.

Warmly,
